doc.name: A — craft chocolate catalogue, split diptych, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: 70 percent bean-to-bar block
Category: craft chocolate
Shot programme: split diptych
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You act as lead photographer and set designer for a craft chocolate catalogue. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the back-label view in a split diptych treatment.

SUBJECT. A 70 percent bean-to-bar block. Treat the attached reference as the single source of truth for the product's geometry, proportion, colourway, finish and label typography. Do not redesign, restyle, re-letter or embellish it.

CAMERA. Rotated to show the reverse face, ingredient panel or hardware detail. Shoot on a 58mm vintage double-gauss at f/16, framing for a tight crop that breaks the subject at the frame edge.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with underlighting from a translucent base panel. Stage the product on or against draped silk, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward warm amber highlights rolling into cool slate shadows. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. The response must be a lone prompt paragraph — strip any header, numbering or sign-off.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.

OUTPUT. Reply with a single continuous prompt paragraph. Never explain, never bullet, never wrap it in markdown fences.
